items.text: Two weeks without Wednesdays — containers don’t keep. They are rebuilt every time, by the same small faithful steps
“Tonight we open it slowly, on purpose. Don’t rush the steps. There is nowhere else we need to be.”
The full eight steps — phones away, standing circle, put out / bring in, the prayer
One-word check-in: “One word for how you actually are right now — not how you usually are, not how you should be.” Let each word have a breath

panel.label: THE SPOKEN COMMITMENT
lines: “I am here. I am paying attention. I am willing to be moved.”

items.text: Written in the ashes of Jerusalem — the mercies-new truth lives in the mornings after the seasons that didn’t hold
Not new every morning that you earned. Issued fresh, this morning, to everyone in this circle — whatever the break looked like
Psalm 126 — “those who sow in tears shall reap with shouts of joy!” Coming home is not make-up work; it is the happiest walk there is
Tonight we read the break honestly — and we can afford to, because the mercy was already new before we walked in

panel.label: LAMENTATIONS 3:22–23
lines: “The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases; his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.”

items.text: A reading, not a report card — which practices held through the break, and which slipped
“Every break is a natural test, and it is a test of the practices, not of you.”
One at a time, plain words — a parent starts in each cluster
Nobody fixes anybody. Nobody compares. Slips are data — useful information, not a verdict
“Most of it slipped” is a complete answer; pass is a complete answer
If time allows: “Did anything about the break surprise you?”
The Path Home Card — filed weeks ago, while the room was warm. Tonight it is not taught; it is enacted
“Nobody in this room owes anybody an explanation for the break. You already walked back. You are in the chair. That is the whole return.”
The way back is unglamorous: do not start over from the beginning; begin again on the next available day. Five dry minutes tomorrow morning is a full return
Everybody here came back — every chair filled tonight is a small feast
If the break was hard in ways that have nothing to do with practices — that is a Companion conversation, tonight or this week

panel.label: LUKE 15:20
lines: “But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and felt compassion, and ran and embraced him and kissed him.”

items.text: Behind us: the whole God arc — the container, your story, the soils, being known; then the hearing: PROAPT, the garden, the doubts brought honestly
“That work is in you now. The break did not take it away.”
Ahead: Week 13 — Mission, the turn outward; then the Rhythm — one card you build with your own hand; then the sendings and the commissionings
“We are not starting over tonight. We are picking the trail back up, together, further along than we have ever been.”
Not everything. One daily practice — the morning question, the evening note, or PROAPT. Just one
Write it at the top of a fresh journal page tonight, with when and where: “The morning question, 6:50, kitchen table”
That one practice, daily, this week
Miss a day? Do not start over — begin again on the next available day
“One seed goes back in the ground. His mercies are new every morning; you only need one practice to be standing there when they arrive.”
